subject: Maths
title: Equations with brackets
subtitle: Solving Linear Equations · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can solve linear equations that involve expanding brackets.

key_vocab.definition: When an equation contains brackets, expand them first, then collect like terms and solve as normal. Remember to multiply every term inside the bracket.

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can solve linear equations that involve expanding brackets.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: brackets -- When an equation contains brackets, expand them first, then collect like terms and solve as normal. Remember to multiply every term inside the bracket.

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Expand all brackets first, then solve by collecting like terms.
a(x + b) = c ⇒ ax + ab = c
Multiply every term inside by the number outside

Key examples:
  ✓ 2(x + 3) = 10 ⇒ 2x + 6 = 10 ⇒ x = 2  (expand then solve)
  ✓ 3(2x − 1) = 15 ⇒ 6x − 3 = 15 ⇒ x = 3  (multiply both terms)
  ✓ 5(x + 2) = 3(x + 6) ⇒ 5x + 10 = 3x + 18 ⇒ x = 4  (brackets both sides)
  ✗ 2(x + 3) = 2x + 3  (must multiply both terms: 2x + 6)
  ✗ 3(2x − 1) = 6x − 1  (must multiply the −1 too: 6x − 3)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – single bracket
  Solve 3(x + 4) = 21
  Expand: 3x + 12 = 21
  Subtract 12: 3x = 9
  Divide by 3: x = 3
  x = 3
  (Expand first, then use inverse operations to isolate x.)

Example 2 – bracket with subtraction
  Solve 4(2x − 3) = 20
  Expand: 8x − 12 = 20
  Add 12: 8x = 32
  Divide by 8: x = 4
  x = 4
  (Remember to multiply the negative term too: 4 × (−3) = −12.)

teacher_sections.title: Teacher Key & Mark Scheme
teacher_sections.content:
Award marks for correct working and final answers.

Single bracket:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 3
  (c) x = 5
  (d) x = 5

Coefficient of x not 1:
  (a) x = 2
  (b) x = 4
  (c) x = 2
  (d) x = 3

Brackets on both sides:
  (a) x = 4
  (b) x = 7
  (c) x = 9
  (d) x = 7

Negative outside bracket:
  (a) x = 5
  (b) x = 5
  (c) x = 5
  (d) x = 2

Mixed bracket equations:
  (a) x = 3
  (b) x = 3
  (c) x = 5
  (d) x = 3
  (e) x = 4
